audits.title: Insulin prescribing, administration, and glucose monitoring trends in Irish hospitals: scope for improvement?
audits.standard: Local insulin prescribing, administration and glucose monitoring standards

cycle1.result: 90% [37] of insulin-prescribed inpatients had one or more errors; 95% brand names and 89% dose units clearly prescribed; 87% orders signed; 70% administrations double checked; 26% [10] given insulin when not prescribed.

audits.other_findings: 454 inpatients reviewed, 41 on insulin; only 58% of prescribers documented contact details and 35% of meal time supplements were documented clearly; results to inform QI initiatives.
audits.citation: Hogan-Murphy D, Reddington L, Dennedy MC, Egan L, Okiro J, Given J, et al.. Insulin prescribing, administration, and glucose monitoring trends in Irish hospitals: scope for improvement?. . 2022. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-1709483/v1.

audits.title: MEASURE IT, IMPROVE IT: the Safer Patients Initiative and quality improvement in subcutaneous insulin therapy for hospital in-patients.
audits.standard: Evidence-based care cluster for subcutaneous insulin therapy

cycle1.result: Baseline: patient identification 97%; insulin device identification 11%; insulin administration 75%; hypoglycaemic control 85%.

audits.intervention: New insulin prescribing chart based on an evidence-based care cluster, refined through PDSA cycles, with run charts fed back to staff

cycle2.result: Patient identification 100%; insulin device identification 100%; insulin administration 95%; hypoglycaemic control 94%.

audits.other_findings: Chart also created opportunities to educate non-specialist staff.
audits.citation: Rushmer R, Voigt D. MEASURE IT, IMPROVE IT: the Safer Patients Initiative and quality improvement in subcutaneous insulin therapy for hospital in-patients. Diabet Med. 2008;25(8):960-967. doi:10.1111/j.1464-5491.2008.02470.x. PMID: 18959610.

audits.title: Facilitating the safe use of insulin pens in hospitals through a mentored quality-improvement program.
audits.setting: Interprofessional teams at 14 US hospitals in an ASHP mentored quality improvement programme

cycle1.result: Baseline nurse knowledge, insulin pen storage and labelling audits and injection observations; numbers not reported.

audits.intervention: Distance mentoring by expert pharmacists, continuing education, web resources and site-specific insulin pen quality improvement plans.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in nurse knowledge, pen labelling and storage, and pen administration; figures not reported.

audits.other_findings: Sample is number of hospitals; authors stress sustained organisational commitment is needed.
audits.citation: Lutz MF, Haines ST, Lesch CA, Szumita PM. Facilitating the safe use of insulin pens in hospitals through a mentored quality-improvement program. Am J Health Syst Pharm. 2016;73(19 Suppl 5):S17-31. doi:10.2146/ajhp160417. PMID: 27647095.

audits.title: Development of an Insulin-Prescribing Chart for Paediatric Diabetes
audits.standard: Irish Medicines Safety Network recommendations for insulin prescribing

cycle1.result: Review of 15 consecutive insulin prescribing charts and a staff questionnaire; 50% (17/34) of staff reported confusion with the existing chart.

audits.intervention: New colour-coded paediatric insulin prescribing chart with ALERT system designed and implemented in 2016.

cycle2.result: Confusion reported by 28% (11/39); new chart viewed as easier by 95% of previous users (n=18) and safer (n=16); ALERT system helped standardise hypo/hyperglycaemia management (71%, n=28).

audits.citation: Finn BP, O’Neill T, Bradfield A, O’Sullivan T, Beattie S, O’Connell SM. Development of an Insulin-Prescribing Chart for Paediatric Diabetes. Ir Med J. 2019;112(9):999. PMID: 31651129.

audits.title: An audit of inpatient insulin prescriptions - how error relates to information source.
audits.standard: Accurate inpatient insulin prescription matching the patient's regimen
audits.setting: Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust, inpatients with diabetes

cycle1.result: Only 44/85 (52%) patients or carers recalled being asked about insulin; overall insulin prescription error rate about one in four.

audits.other_findings: Prescription errors were slightly lower when the patient or carer had been asked about their insulin.
audits.citation: Ashley-Fenn W, Janjua Z, Monir S, Yaqub H, Swaray A, Maltese G, et al.. An audit of inpatient insulin prescriptions - how error relates to information source. Future Healthc J. 2024;11(2):100146. doi:10.1016/j.fhj.2024.100146. PMID: 38966834.

audits.title: A prospective re-audit on insulin prescribing and administration practices in a university teaching hospital
audits.setting: Galway University Hospitals; university teaching hospital, 24 wards

cycle1.result: Prescribing errors in 78% (32/41); administration errors 88% (36/41); unsigned orders 12% (5/41); administration times not documented 46% (19/41); no second check 29% (12/41).

audits.intervention: Senior diabetes pharmacist appointed, updated insulin record, eLearning module for high-alert medications and continuous education.

cycle2.result: Prescribing errors 63% (24/38); administration errors 84% (32/38); unsigned orders 21% (8/38); administration times not documented 42% (16/38); no second check 21% (8/38); contact details documented 71% (27/38) vs 59% (24/41).

audits.other_findings: 557 inpatients reviewed, 10% (56/557) prescribed insulin; unsigned orders worsened; ePrescribing under consideration.
audits.citation: Hogan-Murphy D, Cunningham D, Ero A, Uwadoka O, Given J, Cunningham A, et al.. A prospective re-audit on insulin prescribing and administration practices in a university teaching hospital. International Journal of Pharmacy Practice. 2024;32(Supplement_1):i30-i31. doi:10.1093/ijpp/riae013.038.
